identity: Lennie Niehaus: Waltz for Emily, Kendor 11495
findings: Kendor 11495 is the alto saxophone and piano edition; publisher duration 2:10. The preview carries copyright 2011 Coljaco Music, used by Kendor.
Publisher description explicitly addresses young players and developing endurance, with plentiful rests. This is sourced pre-college pedagogical repertoire.
Clarinet edition 11182 is distinct. James Rae's Waltz for Emily in Blue Saxophone is also a different work and should not supply this record's examination or recording data.

evidence.claim: Edition 11495, composer, publisher, duration and intended young audience

evidence.source_name: Kendor public preview hosted by Stanton's

score_observations: First score page:3/4, Giocoso quarter-note≈116, saxophone without key-signature accidentals at opening, piano three flats.

The alto begins after several bars of rest, using mostly sustained, tied and slurred notes with occasional dotted-eighth/sixteenth figures. Opening page includes written upperD/E and later some chromatic pitches.
The viewed passage is lyrical and conventionally notated, with mp/mf dynamics and breath separation. No extended-technique instruction appears in that passage.
collection_flag: Publisher explicitly writes for young players developing endurance. Flag pre-college repertoire; no SaxoBrain year level assigned.
gaps: 2011 is copyright, not a confirmed composition date.
No exact performance recording verified; do not use James Rae recordings.
